messages:
Beth (PM): Quick sync — decided to scope a smaller, testable MVP for the Optimize Advisor pilot. Focus: actionable batching/caching/quant suggestions + eval-alerts. Need concrete launch gates and a customer-ready acceptance doc.
Anna (Eng): I'll call infra constraints: we need lightweight prefix hit telemetry (not full K/V profiler), safe toggle per-route, and canary automation that ties into existing rollback hooks.
Sanjay (ML): From model quality side: we must run quant recs through a canonical prompt set per model family. Recommend shipping recommendations as guidance (score + delta) instead of automated conversion for MVP. ETA: 2.5 weeks for initial harness.
Kai (Solutions): Customer asks: DataScale wants per-route sample configs and runbook; FinServ requires per-model opt-out + KMS audit trail. They both want a simple acceptance checklist they can sign off.
Beth (PM): Proposed acceptance gates: 1) recommendations delivered to API in <250ms for typical route, 2) quant recs show no >2% drop on key eval metrics, 3) pilot customers can enable/disable recs at route level. Agree or adjust? :thinking_face:
Anna (Eng): OK. For the <250ms figure I'll restrict caching to prefix-level caching (TTLed), not response cache. That keeps memory bounded. Also need a config param to cap max_batch to avoid OOMs.
Sanjay (ML): We'll return rec objects like {confidence: 0.82, recommended_quant: "int8", est_throughput: "1.6x", risk_note: "may change logits for rare tokens"}. That keeps it transparent.
Kai (Solutions): Example snippet customers can drop in docs: 
```
optimize_advisor:
  batching:
    max_batch: 12
    batch_window_ms: 8
  caching:
    prefix_cache: true
    prefix_ttl_ms: 45000
  quant_recommendation:
    recommended: "int8"
    confidence: 0.79
```
Beth (PM): Good. Rollout safety — if a recommendation is applied and we see perf/quality regressions, what happens?
Anna (Eng): Canary -> monitor 95p/99p latency and error rate -> auto-rollback if 99p latency increases >7% or error rate +3 percentage points. Expose thresholds as runtime flags so SOs can tune.
Sanjay (ML): Add eval-triggered alerts: whenever a model/quant change causes regression >threshold on canonical sets, flag rec as "manual review required" and post to #pilot-ops.
Beth (PM): Scope: what's must-have vs nice-to-have for MVP?
Anna (Eng): Must: prefix cache telemetry, per-route toggle, canary automation + rollback hooks. Nice: per-tenant default profiles, UI in Console.
Sanjay (ML): Must: eval harness + seed prompt sets, quant heuristics. Nice: continuous auto-tuning loop.
Kai (Solutions): Must: customer docs + acceptance checklist. Nice: one-click import into Dedicated configs.
Beth (PM): Timeline suggestion: scope lock by Friday, 2-week dev spike, first internal pilot by week 4, external pilot with DataScale/FinServ by week 6. Concerns?
Anna (Eng): Spike is fine, but we need an extra SRE/infra head for canary automation to hit week 4.
Sanjay (ML): ML evals line up with spike + 2 weeks. Good.
Beth (PM): Action items: @Anna list infra tasks and owner; @Sanjay publish prompt sets and run plan; @Kai draft customer acceptance doc and sample configs. I'll compile the Launch Gate doc and schedule a 15m follow-up tomorrow.
Devex Bot: Created issue OPT-RECS-812: https://redwood.example/issue/OPT-RECS-812 — add estimates, owners, and link PRs.
Kai (Solutions): Drafting acceptance checklist now, will ping for review.
Beth (PM): Thanks all — aim to keep MVP lean and observable. :rocket:
